segments.he: בִּפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין וְשֶׁלֹּא בִּפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין כּוּ׳. בְּמַאי קָמִיפַּלְגִי?
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: The oath of testimony is practiced both «in the presence of» the «court and not in the presence of» the «court,» when the potential witness takes the oath on his own. And if the oath is administered by others he is liable only when he denies, in court, any knowledge of the incident in question. This is the statement of Rabbi Meir. And the Rabbis say: Whether the witness takes the oath on his own or whether the oath is administered by others, he is liable only when he denies, in court, any knowledge of the incident in question. The Gemara asks: «With regard to what do they disagree?»
